items.title: EBRD and GCF scale up support for greener cities
items.one_liner: The EBRD and the Green Climate Fund are scaling up their joint financial support programs for greener cities.
items.why: Directly relevant to funding models for urban ecosystem services and green infrastructure in developing regions.
items.action: Check eligibility criteria and project types covered under the expanded EBRD-GCF greener cities initiative.

items.title: Six paradigm shifts for Global South cities sustainability
items.one_liner: A new publication outlines six paradigm shifts that could redefine how Global South cities plan for sustainability.
items.why: Directly aligns with the student's focus on urban planning and environmental frameworks in Global South cities like Kabul.
items.action: Locate and review the core publication detailing the six proposed paradigm shifts for planning.

items.title: Nature-based solutions for flood protection in Europe
items.one_liner: An overview highlights how nature-based solutions could help protect Europe from severe flooding.
items.why: Connects to green-blue infrastructure and stormwater retention strategies relevant to urban environmental planning.
items.action: Read the report to see which specific nature-based solutions are highlighted for flood risk reduction.

items.title: UN report: Rich countries fall short on adaptation funding
items.one_liner: A UN report states that wealthy nations are falling far short on delivering necessary climate adaptation funding.
items.why: Highlights macro-level financial constraints affecting climate resilience and adaptation in vulnerable regions.
items.action: Check the UN report details on adaptation funding gaps to ground the student's financing context.

items.title: UNEP warns adaptation is too slow amid 1.5°C overshoot
items.one_liner: UNEP warns that as the world heads for a 1.5°C temperature overshoot, urban and global adaptation is proceeding too slowly.
items.why: Reinforces the urgency of integrating rapid heat mitigation and urban cooling into planning frameworks.
items.action: Review the UNEP findings regarding overshoot risks and slow urban adaptation paces.

items.title: McKinsey Global Institute climate adaptation funding
items.one_liner: McKinsey Global Institute reports that climate adaptation needs $1.2 trillion yearly by 2050, with $690 billion stuck.
items.why: Provides economic data on the massive global shortfall in climate adaptation and resilience investments.
items.action: Incorporate these economic metrics into discussions on urban resilience financing bottlenecks.

items.title: EBRD €62.9M financing for Muğla water infrastructure
items.one_liner: Dentons advised EBRD on €62.9 million in financing dedicated to water infrastructure in Muğla.
items.why: Provides a concrete example of international financial institution backing for urban water and infrastructure.
items.action: Analyze the financial structure used by the EBRD for municipal water projects.

items.title: Funding secured for greener urban spaces
items.one_liner: New funding has been successfully secured to develop greener urban spaces in the Brimbank and North West region.
items.why: Demonstrates practical financial mechanisms for urban greening projects which can inform comparative case studies.
items.action: Investigate the funding sources and deployment models used for these urban greening initiatives.

items.title: NZ resource management rules rewritten
items.one_liner: New Zealand's resource management rules have been rewritten following recent political developments.
items.why: Offers comparative perspective on national-level statutory changes affecting resource management and planning.
items.action: Examine the specific changes made to resource management rules to evaluate planning implications.

items.title: CLEW Guide on EU Net-Zero Legislation
items.one_liner: A new Clean Energy Wire guide details how the European Union is trying to legislate a path to net-zero.
items.why: Provides relevant context on European statutory frameworks and environmental policy instruments.
items.action: Review the guide to extract transferable insights on how legal mandates shape urban climate targets.

note: Selected updates, not comprehensive coverage. Status is unverified unless supported by the quoted official excerpt.
